inventory.interpretation: All /Subj, /Contents, and /T fields were scanned for every Issue #N marker. This reproduces the /Subj-only set: 165 unique IDs and 516 issue-marked annotations, no annotation with multiple IDs, and no IDs found only outside /Subj. Of the 516 annotations, 144 have /IRT; they are issue-marked annotations, not necessarily roots. Counts are exact textual references matching #N, not coverage verdicts. Many annotations map to source behavior already reviewed without the Issue ID citation. No ID mismatch alone is a defect. Compact issue annotation/reply/status and annotation-shape data is in issues.json; full Contents bodies are intentionally not copied.

It qualifies public-key key-derivation step (c): the 0xFF bytes apply only to the document-level key for the default StmF crypt filter when that filter's EncryptMetadata is false; s3/s4 have no crypt-filter way to leave metadata plaintext, so step (c) is skipped.

reviewed_candidates.mapping: No explicit Issue #25 citation found in the old feature ledger or current shard text. The current public-key shard reviews the file-key path and its AES128/AES256 ExposedMeta witnesses, which exercise a default-stream EncryptMetadata=false case. Code in crates/pdf-syntax/src/crypt/public_key.rs gates the flag on from_stream and encrypt_metadata; s3/s4 set the flag true; own per-stream keys call file_key with the metadata flag false. No contrary behavior found. This annotation is substantially behavior-covered without ID-level attribution; no defect established.

reviewed_candidates.mapping: No explicit Issue #114 citation in the old feature ledger or current shard text. Table 16 has an aggregate row for Type/N/First but no distinct entry-value representation row. The serializer's flush writes Type, N, First, Filter, Length directly and Extends as a reference to an ordinary uncompressed stream, so its emitted dictionary meets the rule by construction. Reader get_key resolves indirect values, but the inspected object-stream tests use direct N/First/Length; a valid indirect-uncompressed positive fixture is a meaningful assertion gap. This is not a malformed-input rejection defect. See draft for /N, /First, and /Length references to top-level uncompressed integer objects, with an exact xref stream and reachable page-tree result.
